learningObjectives: Identify the three scenarios that require Dev Studio Validate Rules or Edit Validate Rules instead of App Studio.
Distinguish Validate Rules from Edit Validate Rules — scope, timing, and how they relate.
Configure input-qualified Validate Rules using the four Input tab qualification types.

elements.text: Receptionist vs. Compliance Officer — A receptionist (App Studio) asks one question: 'Is your name on the list — yes or no?' A compliance officer (Dev Studio) checks the format of your ID, applies different rules based on your clearance level, and demands extra documents only at certain checkpoints. Same goal — very different capabilities.

elements.description: Validation Conditions compare one field against a constant or another field. Example: Income > 10,000? StartDate before EndDate? Anything beyond binary comparison requires Dev Studio.

elements.term: Validate Rule — Case-level, fires on form submit
elements.description: Ensures data meets Case conditions before it advances. Assigned to Flow Actions. In Dev Studio you can extend App Studio-created rules or create new ones in the Process category.

elements.term: Edit Validate Rule — property-level, Java, client-side
elements.description: Compares a property value to a defined pattern using Java code. Example: check whether a value consists of seven numbers with a space between the 3rd and 4th digits. Fires immediately on value change — before form submit.

elements.term: Two ways to apply an Edit Validate Rule
elements.description: ① Advanced tab of the property rule form → 'Use Validate' field — fires on value change (client-side). ② Call it from a Validate Rule — fires on form submit (server-side). The second is preferred for coordinated validation logic.

elements.term: Use Case 1 — Format validation by business logic
elements.description: When input must match a location-specific pattern (postal code, email, phone). Example: US ZIP code must be exactly 5 numerical digits. → Edit Validate Rule called FROM a Validate Rule (not applied directly to the property here).

elements.term: Use Case 2 — Different rules per input value
elements.description: When validation logic depends on user selection. Example: experienced investors can add margin trading (low risk); limited experience = high risk; retirement accounts prohibit margin regardless. Use Validate Rule + Input tab qualification on experience and account type.

Dev Studio's Validate Rule provides a library of Validation Functions with customized configuration fields. Examples: check if a date falls within the past 4 or 8 weeks; check if a specific attachment category is attached.

elements.term: Input Property — qualify by user-entered value
elements.description: Applies a different validation set per value the user selected. Example: Experience level = 'Extensive' → validate broker license; 'Limited' → validate suitability score.

elements.term: Proposed Work Status — qualify by Case Status
elements.description: Applies different thresholds per Case Status. Example: Pending-Qualification → credit score ≥ 600; Approved → credit score ≥ 725.

elements.term: Flow Action — qualify by the user's action
elements.description: Applies different validation per triggered action. Example: 'Onboard Employee' → start date must be in the future; 'Annual Review' → must be in the past.

elements.term: Stages — qualify by current Stage ★ also in App Studio
elements.description: Applies different validation per Stage. Example: Submission → estimated income OK; Approval → confirmed value required. Only qualifier available in BOTH Dev Studio and App Studio (as Stage-entry Validation).

examPitfalls.title: App Studio cannot do format or function-based validation
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask whether App Studio supports all validation types. Candidates say yes. App Studio supports simple property-level validation; format validation and function-based validation require Dev Studio — they cannot be configured in App Studio.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: App Studio supports true/false comparisons only. Format checks and function-based operations always require Dev Studio.

examPitfalls.title: Edit Validate Rules are client-side — NOT server-side
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks when Edit Validate rule logic executes. Candidates say 'on the server when the form is submitted.' Edit Validate rules execute client-side in the browser — they provide immediate feedback without a server round-trip.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Edit Validate Rules fire on value change (client-side). Exception: when called from a Validate Rule, they fire on form submit instead.

examPitfalls.title: Edit Validate Rules are property-level — not Case-level
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask the scope of an Edit Validate rule. Candidates say 'the entire Case.' Each Edit Validate rule is associated with a single property — it validates that property's value, not the Case as a whole.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Edit Validate Rules target individual properties (e.g., the postal code field). Validate Rules operate at Case/process level.

examPitfalls.title: Two application methods for Edit Validate Rules — know both
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks how to apply an Edit Validate rule to a property. Candidates describe only one method. Edit Validate rules can be applied via the property definition OR via the field configuration in a View — both are valid and tested.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: ① Property Advanced tab → 'Use Validate' field (fires on change). ② Call from a Validate Rule (fires on submit). Both are valid; the second is preferred for coordinated logic.

examPitfalls.title: Stages is the ONLY qualifier also available in App Studio — the other 3 are Dev Studio-only
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask which Input tab qualifiers are exclusive to Dev Studio. Candidates include Stages. The four qualifiers (Stages, Role, Skill, Routing) differ: Stages can also be set in App Studio — the other three (Role, Skill, Routing) require Dev Studio.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Stages → configurable in App Studio as Stage-entry Validation. Input Property, Proposed Work Status, and Flow Action → Dev Studio ONLY. On an exam question asking 'which is available in both?' — answer is always Stages.

examPitfalls.title: Memorize all 4 Input tab qualifiers
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask for a complete list of Input tab qualifiers for a property. Candidates list only two or three. There are exactly four: Stages, Role, Skill, and Routing — memorize all four for the exam.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: ① Input Property → by user-entered value. ② Proposed Work Status → by Case Status. ③ Flow Action → by user's action. ④ Stages → by current Stage.

examPitfalls.title: Edit Validate Rules carry security risk due to custom Java
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks why Edit Validate rules require careful governance. Candidates say 'performance risk only.' Edit Validate rules can contain custom Java code — this introduces security risk if the code is not reviewed, making governance and code review essential.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Custom Java = potential security risk. Prefer Pega's built-in Edit Validate Rules over creating new ones. Use the function library in Validate Rules when possible.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A US address form must validate that the postal code is exactly 5 numerical digits. Which Pega mechanism handles this?

options.text: Edit Validate Rule — Java code compares the property value to the 5-digit pattern
App Studio validation condition — compare the postal code to a constant
Stage validation — validates the format before the Case advances
Field Type = Numeric — restricts input to digits automatically

practiceQuiz.hint: Format check by business logic = Edit Validate Rule.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Format/pattern checks require an Edit Validate Rule — Java code that compares the property value to the required pattern. App Studio only does true/false comparisons; Field Type doesn't enforce a specific count.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega System Architect is deciding between App Studio validation and Dev Studio Validate Rules for a new Claims application and needs to understand what kind of validation logic App Studio can natively configure. What type of data validation does App Studio support?

options.text: True/false comparisons — field vs. constant or field vs. field
Format validation using pattern matching on property values
Input-qualified validation — different rules per user-entered value
Attachment-presence checks using the function library

practiceQuiz.hint: App Studio validation = simple binary comparison only.
practiceQuiz.rationale: App Studio Validation Conditions support only true/false comparisons — no patterns, functions, or qualification. Anything more complex (B, C, D) requires configuring a Validate Rule in Dev Studio.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An investment account Case must apply different validation rules based on the investor's 'Experience level' selection. Which configuration enables this?

options.text: Validate Rule + 'Input property' on the Input tab — a separate validation set per level
Two separate Validate Rules — one per experience level, triggered by a When Rule
Decision Table that routes to different validation flows
App Studio validation condition comparing the experience level field

practiceQuiz.hint: Different rules per user-selected value = Input property qualifier.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Input property qualifier on a Validate Rule's Input tab creates separate validation sets per property value. B is not the documented approach; C routes work, not validates; D can't handle conditional logic like this.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How does an Edit Validate Rule differ from a standard Validate Rule in timing?

options.text: Edit Validate Rules fire on value change (client-side); Validate Rules fire on form submit (server-side)
Edit Validate Rules fire on form submit; Validate Rules fire on value change
Both fire at the same time — difference is only in what they check
Edit Validate Rules fire only when the Case advances to a new Stage

practiceQuiz.hint: Edit = client-side (immediate change). Validate Rule = server-side (submit).
practiceQuiz.rationale: Edit Validate Rules validate client-side on value change. Validate Rules fire server-side on form submit. Exception: when called from a Validate Rule, the Edit Validate Rule fires on submit too.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA wants to apply an Edit Validate Rule to a property so validation fires as the user types. Where is it referenced?

options.text: Advanced tab of the property rule form → 'Use Validate' field
Validation tab of the Flow Action rule
Input tab of the Validate Rule
Settings tab of the Case Type in App Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: Direct property-level application = Advanced tab → Use Validate.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Applying an Edit Validate Rule directly to a property (fires on change) uses the Advanced tab of the property rule → 'Use Validate' field. The Validation tab (B) is for assigning a Validate Rule to a Flow Action.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Validate Rule must only apply when the Case Status is 'Pending-Qualification'. Which Input tab qualifier enables this?

options.text: Proposed work status
Input property
Flow Action
Stages

practiceQuiz.hint: Case Status on a Validate Rule represents proposed work status, not the actual current status.
practiceQuiz.rationale: In Dev Studio's Validate Rule, the 'Qualifies when' setting controls when the rule fires. Four qualify-by options exist: Proposed work status (triggers on Case Status), Input property (triggers on a specific field value entered by the user), Flow Action (triggers on a particular user action), and Stage (triggers based on the current Stage of the Case). Each targets a different runtime context.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A mortgage Case requires estimated income during 'Submission' Stage, but confirmed income during 'Approval'. Which qualifier handles this?

options.text: Stages — different validation sets per Stage
Proposed work status — different thresholds per Case Status
Flow Action — validates based on the action triggered
Input property — validates based on income value entered

practiceQuiz.hint: Which Input tab qualifier makes a validation rule apply only during a specific Stage?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Qualify a Validate Rule to a specific Flow Action so validation only fires when the user takes that Action. Without qualification, the Rule fires on all submissions at that Step.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A SA is deciding when to use Dev Studio's Edit Validate Rules instead of App Studio validation. Which TWO scenarios require the use of Dev Studio validation rather than App Studio validation?

options.text: Validate a postal code matches a country-specific format pattern
Validate that Annual Income is greater than $10,000
Validate that a specific attachment category is attached to the Case
Validate that a Start date field is not empty

practiceQuiz.hint: Format patterns and Validation Function-based checks need Dev Studio.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A requires an Edit Validate Rule called from a Validate Rule (Java pattern match). C requires a Validation Function from Dev Studio's function library. B and D are simple true/false comparisons App Studio can handle.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A lead SA is reviewing the team's validation approach and cautions against overusing Edit Validate Rules with custom Java. Why do Edit Validate Rules with custom Java code represent a potential security risk?

options.text: They contain custom Java code that can introduce vulnerabilities
They execute server-side and expose internal data
They are not version-controlled in Pega's ruleset
They bypass Pega's access control model

practiceQuiz.hint: The risk = custom Java in the application.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Edit Validate Rules that include custom Java code introduce potential security vulnerabilities — such as injection risks or unintended access to system APIs — because Pega executes the custom code as part of form submission. Unlike declarative Rules, custom Java bypasses some of Pega's built-in safety layers, requiring careful code review and auditing by security-conscious SAs.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Validate Rule must apply only when the user triggers 'Run Annual Review' — not 'Onboard Employee'. Which qualifier?

options.text: Flow Action
Input property
Proposed work status
Stages

practiceQuiz.hint: Qualify validation to fire only on the specific user Flow Action at that Step.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Flow Action qualifies by which action the user triggered. Input property = by entered value; Proposed work status = by Case Status; Stages = by current Stage.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA calls an Edit Validate Rule from a Validate Rule. When does the validation fire?

options.text: When the user submits the form — the Validate Rule runs and triggers the Edit Validate Rule
Immediately when the user types in the field — client-side
When the Case advances to the next Stage
When the Case is first created

practiceQuiz.hint: Called from Validate Rule = fires when Validate Rule runs = on form submit.
practiceQuiz.rationale: When an Edit Validate Rule is called from a Validate Rule, it fires on form submit — not on value change. Applying it directly to a property (via Use Validate) is what fires on value change.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Of the four Input tab qualification types, which ONE can also be configured in App Studio?

options.text: Input property
Proposed work status
Flow Action
Stages

practiceQuiz.hint: Stage-entry Validation exists in App Studio — that's your clue.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Stages (D) can be configured in App Studio as Stage-entry Validation. Input property, Proposed work status, and Flow Action are all Dev Studio-only qualifier types.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer is deciding between App Studio validation and Dev Studio Edit Validate Rules. Which TWO statements correctly describe Edit Validate Rules in Pega?

options.text: Edit Validate Rules run whenever a property value is set or changed, regardless of which form or process triggers the change
Edit Validate Rules are property-level rules that apply consistently wherever that property is used in the application
Edit Validate Rules execute only during an Assignment step and are ignored during automated processing tasks
Edit Validate Rules completely replace Validate Rules and cannot be used alongside them in the same application

practiceQuiz.hint: Edit Validate Rules are property-level and fire on every change to that property — not just at form submission.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Edit Validate Rules are attached to a specific property and execute every time that property's value is set or modified, regardless of the trigger (form submission, automation, or data transform). Because they are property-level, they apply consistently across all forms and processes that use that property. They complement, rather than replace, Validate Rules.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer has configured a Validate Rule with an Input qualification. Which TWO statements about input-qualified Validate Rules are correct?

options.text: The Input tab specifies which properties must hold specific values for the Validate Rule to be applied
An input-qualified Validate Rule fires only when its qualifying conditions are met — it is skipped otherwise
Input qualification always requires exactly three qualifying conditions — no more, no fewer
Input qualification prevents the Validate Rule from running during any automated processing task

practiceQuiz.hint: Input qualification is a conditional gate on the Validate Rule — it fires only when qualifying property values match.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Input tab on a Validate Rule defines qualification conditions — specific property values that must be present for the rule to execute. When those conditions are not met, the rule is skipped entirely.

quickRecap.value: True/false only — field vs. constant or field vs. field.
Format by business logic (ZIP = 5 digits) → Edit Validate Rule.
Different rules per input value → Validate Rule + Input tab (Input property qualifier).
Beyond true/false → Validate Rule + Validation Function library. Examples: date within past 4/8 weeks; attachment category attached to Case.
Case-level. Server-side. Fires on form submit. Assigned to Flow Actions.
Property-level. Java code. Client-side (fires on value change). Security risk.
① Property → Advanced tab → Use Validate (fires on change). ② From Validate Rule (fires on submit).
① Input property → by value entered. ② Proposed work status → by Case Status. ③ Flow Action → by action. ④ Stages → by Stage.
Only qualifier also available in App Studio (as Stage-entry Validation).
